items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear, but durability.go tracker fields and the waiter struct (`active`, `isJob`) have no comments. applyInternal has a long nested block with no comments that sets durations to `time.Nanosecond` with no explanation.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: applyInternal grew to about 145 lines (db.go L790-L934), over the 100-line cap. The BatchDurableInfo construction and nanosecond clamping are copy-pasted into both branches. durability.go is 563 lines. The reflect-pointer `hasBatchDurable` check is a hack.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: commitWrite replaced `panic(err)` with `err = nil`. A WAL WriteRecord failure on a non-sync commit (syncWG nil) is now silently swallowed on a data-mutation path. It also hand-drains `<-d.commit.logSyncQSem`. Every NoSyncWait sync commit spawns an untracked goroutine.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: Changes existing commit behavior: `Logger.Fatalf` on a commit error became `return commitErr`, the WAL write panics were removed, and Batch.SeqNum() now returns a cached seqNum. Every Sync commit takes the tracker mutex even when BatchDurable is unset. NoSyncWait commits now spawn a goroutine each.
